cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: A time series is a sequence of data values collected at regular time intervals (e.g. monthly sales, quarterly temperatures).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: The trend is the long-term general direction of the data, ignoring short-term fluctuations; it can be increasing, decreasing, or stationary.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: Seasonal variation is a regular, repeating pattern that occurs at fixed periods within a year (e.g. higher ice cream sales in summer).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: Cyclical variation is a longer-term pattern that repeats over more than one year (e.g. economic boom and bust cycles); it is harder to predict than seasonal variation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: A moving average smooths out short-term fluctuations to reveal the underlying trend; it is calculated by averaging overlapping groups of consecutive data values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: A 4-point moving average is used for quarterly data; each average covers four consecutive quarters and is centred between the middle two quarters.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: Because a 4-point moving average falls between two time periods, a second set of 2-point moving averages (centred moving averages) is needed to align with actual time periods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: To calculate a centred 4-point moving average: first find the 4-point totals, then find the mean of each pair of consecutive 4-point averages.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: The seasonal variation for a quarter = actual value – trend value (from the centred moving average); positive means above trend, negative means below trend.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: The mean seasonal variation for each quarter is found by averaging all the seasonal variations for that specific quarter across different years.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: To make a prediction: estimate the trend (e.g. by extending the moving average line), then add the appropriate mean seasonal variation for the quarter.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Time Series Moving Averages
cards.back: Predictions based on time series assume that past patterns will continue; they become less reliable the further into the future they are made.

cards.back: 1. For Time Series & Moving Averages questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2.
